column1: Search Insert Position — given sorted array `nums` and `target`, return the index where target is found, or where it would be inserted to keep the array sorted. Example: [1,3,5,6], 5 → 2; [1,3,5,6], 2 → 1; [1,3,5,6], 7 → 4.
column2: PATTERN: Standard lower-bound binary search. | INSIGHT: Search for the leftmost index with nums[i]>=target; the loop converges to insertion index. | STEPS: 1) lo=0, hi=n. 2) While lo<hi: m=(lo+hi)//2; if nums[m]<target: lo=m+1; else hi=m. 3) Return lo. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Use hi=n (one past the end) to support insertion at the end.

column1: Search a 2D Matrix — m×n matrix where each row is sorted and the first int of each row is greater than the last of the previous row; return True if `target` exists. Example: matrix=[[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target=3 → True.
column2: PATTERN: Treat 2D as 1D and binary search. | INSIGHT: Row-major flattened array of size m·n is fully sorted. | STEPS: 1) lo=0, hi=m*n. 2) While lo<hi: mid=(lo+hi)//2; v=matrix[mid//n][mid%n]; if v==target: True; if v<target: lo=mid+1; else hi=mid. 3) Return False. | TIME/SPACE: O(log mn) / O(1). | PITFALL: Index conversion: row=mid//n, col=mid%n.

column1: Find Peak Element — given int array, return the index of any peak element (strictly greater than both neighbors; out-of-bound treated as -inf). Must run in O(log n). Example: [1,2,3,1] → 2; [1,2,1,3,5,6,4] → 1 or 5.
column2: PATTERN: Binary search on slope. | INSIGHT: If nums[m]<nums[m+1], a peak must lie in the right half (slope rising); otherwise left half (slope falling or peak here). | STEPS: 1) lo=0, hi=n-1. 2) While lo<hi: m=(lo+hi)//2; if nums[m]<nums[m+1]: lo=m+1; else hi=m. 3) Return lo. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Compare nums[m] to nums[m+1] (slope), not to a target.

column1: Search in Rotated Sorted Array — sorted distinct array rotated at an unknown pivot; return index of target or -1, in O(log n). Example: [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], target=0 → 4; target=3 → -1.
column2: PATTERN: Modified binary search — one half is always sorted. | INSIGHT: At any midpoint, exactly one of the two halves is fully sorted. Decide which half via nums[lo]<=nums[m]; check whether target lies in that sorted half. | STEPS: 1) lo=0, hi=n-1. 2) While lo<=hi: m=(lo+hi)//2; if nums[m]==target: return m. If nums[lo]<=nums[m]: (left sorted) if nums[lo]<=target<nums[m]: hi=m-1; else lo=m+1. Else: (right sorted) if nums[m]<target<=nums[hi]: lo=m+1; else hi=m-1. 3) Return -1. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: The nums[lo]<=nums[m] inclusive comparison and inclusive bounds are easy to flip.

column1: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array — given sorted `nums` and `target`, return [first_idx, last_idx] (or [-1,-1] if absent) in O(log n). Example: [5,7,7,8,8,10], target=8 → [3,4]; target=6 → [-1,-1].
column2: PATTERN: Two binary searches (lower bound + upper bound). | INSIGHT: lo = leftmost index with nums[i]>=target; hi = leftmost with nums[i]>target, then hi-1. | STEPS: 1) lo = bisect_left(nums, target). 2) hi = bisect_right(nums, target) - 1. 3) If lo>hi or lo==n or nums[lo]!=target: [-1,-1]. Else [lo, hi]. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Python's bisect_left and bisect_right give you these directly.

column1: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array — sorted DISTINCT array rotated at unknown pivot; return the minimum element in O(log n). Example: [3,4,5,1,2] → 1; [4,5,6,7,0,1,2] → 0.
column2: PATTERN: Binary search comparing mid to RIGHT (not left). | INSIGHT: If nums[m]>nums[hi], the min is in the right half (lo=m+1); else the min is in the left half inclusive (hi=m). | STEPS: 1) lo=0, hi=n-1. 2) While lo<hi: m=(lo+hi)//2; if nums[m]>nums[hi]: lo=m+1; else hi=m. 3) Return nums[lo]. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Compare to nums[hi], not nums[lo] — comparing to lo fails when the array isn't rotated at all.

column1: Median of Two Sorted Arrays — given two sorted arrays of sizes m and n, return the median in O(log(min(m,n))). Example: nums1=[1,3], nums2=[2] → 2.0; [1,2],[3,4] → 2.5.
column2: PATTERN: Binary search on the partition of the SHORTER array. | INSIGHT: Find partition i in A and j=(m+n+1)/2 - i in B such that max(left side) ≤ min(right side); median computed from the boundary values. | STEPS: 1) Ensure A is the shorter array. 2) lo=0, hi=m. While lo<=hi: i=(lo+hi)//2; j=(m+n+1)//2 - i. Aleft=A[i-1] or -inf; Aright=A[i] or +inf; Bleft=B[j-1] or -inf; Bright=B[j] or +inf. If Aleft<=Bright and Bleft<=Aright: total even → (max(Aleft,Bleft)+min(Aright,Bright))/2; odd → max(Aleft,Bleft). Else if Aleft>Bright: hi=i-1; else lo=i+1. | TIME/SPACE: O(log min(m,n)) / O(1). | PITFALL: Use ±inf sentinels to avoid edge-case index spaghetti.
